title: Bounded Blocking Queue (Lock + Two Conditions)
prompt:
Implement a thread-safe, fixed-capacity FIFO queue that blocks producers when full and consumers when empty.

```java
class BoundedBlockingQueue<T> {
  BoundedBlockingQueue(int capacity);
  void put(T item) throws InterruptedException;                  // blocks while full
  T take() throws InterruptedException;                          // blocks while empty
  boolean offer(T item, long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws InterruptedException; // false on timeout
  T poll(long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws InterruptedException;                // null on timeout
  int size();
}
```

**Requirements**
- Any number of producer and consumer threads. No item may be lost or delivered twice; size never exceeds capacity.
- Blocking calls must respond to interruption by throwing `InterruptedException`.
- Timed calls must honor the *total* timeout even across spurious wakeups.
- Null items are rejected with `NullPointerException`.

**Allowed:** `ReentrantLock`, `Condition`, `TimeUnit`. **Not allowed:** any `java.util.concurrent` queue (`ArrayBlockingQueue`, `LinkedBlockingQueue`, ...), `Semaphore`.

**Follow-ups:** Why two conditions instead of one? When would `signal()` be wrong and `signalAll()` required?
complexity: put/take/offer/poll O(1) amortized; O(capacity) memory (ring buffer).
hints: Use a ring buffer (array + head, tail, count) guarded by one ReentrantLock.
Two Conditions: notFull (producers wait) and notEmpty (consumers wait). Always wait in a while loop that re-checks the predicate.
For timeouts use awaitNanos, which returns the remaining time; loop until it is <= 0.
keyPoints: await() always inside while(predicate), never if: handles spurious wakeups and slots stolen by another thread
Separate notFull/notEmpty conditions so signal() wakes a thread that can actually make progress (no lost wakeups)
unlock() in finally; lockInterruptibly() so blocked callers can be cancelled
Timed variants use awaitNanos remaining-time loop rather than restarting the full timeout
Ring buffer nulls out dequeued slots to avoid memory leaks; count kept consistent under the lock

title: Thread-Safe LRU Cache
prompt:
Implement a fixed-capacity least-recently-used cache that is safe to use from many threads.

```java
class LRUCache<K, V> {
  LRUCache(int capacity);
  V get(K key);              // null if absent; marks key most-recently-used
  void put(K key, V value);  // insert or update; evict LRU entry if at capacity
  int size();
}
```

**Requirements**
- O(1) `get` and `put`.
- Under arbitrary concurrent use, the cache never exceeds capacity, never returns a stale value for a key after a completed `put`, and its internal structure never becomes corrupted.

**Allowed:** `HashMap`, `ReentrantLock` / `synchronized`. **Not allowed:** `LinkedHashMap` (build the recency list yourself), `ConcurrentHashMap`, third-party caches.

**Follow-ups:** Why is a ReadWriteLock not a win here? How would you shard the cache to reduce contention, and what does that do to the global LRU guarantee?
complexity: get/put O(1); O(capacity) memory. All operations serialize on one lock.
hints: Classic design: HashMap<K, Node> + doubly linked list with head/tail sentinels.
get() moves the node to the front, so it is a WRITE to the list - it needs the exclusive lock.
To scale, shard into N independent LRU caches by key hash (approximate global LRU).
keyPoints: Recognizes get() mutates recency order, so read locks are unsafe; uses an exclusive lock
Map and list updated together inside one critical section (no window where they disagree)
Eviction removes from both list and map using the node key
Sentinel nodes avoid null checks; unlock in finally
Can discuss striping/sharding and approximate LRU (e.g. sampled or CLOCK) for higher throughput

title: Token-Bucket Rate Limiter (Concurrent Callers)
prompt:
Implement a token-bucket rate limiter safe under concurrent callers.

```java
class TokenBucketRateLimiter {
  TokenBucketRateLimiter(long capacity, double refillPerSecond);
  TokenBucketRateLimiter(long capacity, double refillPerSecond, LongSupplier nanoClock); // for tests
  boolean tryAcquire();             // = tryAcquire(1)
  boolean tryAcquire(int permits);  // non-blocking
  double availableTokens();
}
```

**Requirements**
- The bucket starts full with `capacity` tokens and refills continuously at `refillPerSecond`, never above `capacity`.
- Refill is lazy (computed from elapsed time on each call); no background thread.
- With a frozen clock, if 32 threads race to call `tryAcquire()` thousands of times, **exactly** `capacity` calls succeed.
- Use `System.nanoTime()` (monotonic), not wall-clock time.

**Allowed:** `synchronized`, locks, atomics. **Not allowed:** Guava `RateLimiter`, `Semaphore`.

**Follow-ups:** A lock-free version using a CAS on a packed state; how to rate-limit across many servers (Redis + Lua, or per-node share of a global budget).
hints: State is (tokens, lastRefillNanos). Every call: refill based on now - last, then check-and-decrement.
The refill + check + decrement must be one atomic step, or two threads can both spend the last token.
Inject the clock so the test can freeze/advance time deterministically.
keyPoints: Refill and check-then-act happen atomically (synchronized or a single CAS on combined state)
Uses nanoTime differences, never absolute values; ignores negative elapsed
Caps tokens at capacity; fractional tokens so slow rates still refill
No background refill thread; lazy computation
Validates permits <= capacity (otherwise a request can never succeed)

title: Read-Write-Lock Cache with Single-Flight Loading
complexity: Hit: O(1) under a shared read lock. Miss: O(1) bookkeeping + one loader call per key per flight.
hints: Fast path under the read lock; on a miss take the write lock and re-check (double-checked).
Under the write lock, register an in-flight future for the key if none exists; the thread that registered it is the leader.
The leader runs the loader with no lock held, publishes the value, removes the in-flight entry, then completes the future.
keyPoints: Double-check after upgrading from read to write lock (cannot upgrade a ReentrantReadWriteLock in place)
Exactly one loader per key in flight; followers wait on a shared future
Loader runs outside locks so a slow key does not block other keys or hits
Failure path removes the in-flight entry (allows retry) and propagates the exception to all waiters
Value published before in-flight removal so no window triggers a second load

title: CountDownLatch from Scratch
complexity: countDown O(1) (O(waiters) when it hits zero); await O(1) besides blocking.
hints: Guard the count with the object monitor.
When the count hits zero you must wake every waiter: notifyAll, not notify.
Timed await: compute a deadline once, wait for the remaining time in a loop.
keyPoints: wait() inside while(count > 0): handles spurious wakeups
notifyAll on reaching zero (notify would strand waiters)
Count read/write all under the same monitor (visibility + atomicity)
Deadline-based timed wait; returns false on timeout; propagates InterruptedException
countDown below zero is a no-op

title: Connection Pool with Timed Acquire
complexity: acquire/release O(1) excluding connection creation; O(maxSize) memory.
hints: Track idle (deque), leased (identity set) and created (count, including slots reserved for in-progress creation).
Reserve a slot (created++) under the lock, then create outside the lock; roll back on failure.
Wait on a Condition with awaitNanos in a loop; release() signals one waiter.
keyPoints: Never exceeds maxSize even with concurrent creation (reserve-then-create)
Slow factory call outside the lock; failure releases the reservation and signals
Timed wait loop with awaitNanos; throws TimeoutException precisely when time is up
Double/foreign release detected via identity set
close() uses signalAll so all waiters observe shutdown; fairness discussed (fair lock or FIFO handoff)

title: Striped Counter (LongAdder-Style)
complexity: add: O(1) expected (one CAS, retries move to a different stripe). sum: O(stripes). Memory O(stripes * 64 bytes).
hints: Keep an array of cells and pick one from a hash of the current thread.
Pad cells so two of them never share a 64-byte cache line (e.g. use every 8th slot of an AtomicLongArray).
On CAS failure, try the next stripe instead of hammering the same one.
keyPoints: CAS retry loop (or getAndAdd) per cell: no lost updates
Padding/spacing cells to avoid false sharing; power-of-two masking
Thread-to-stripe hashing spreads threads; contention moves the thread to another cell
Explains sum() is weakly consistent but exact at quiescence
Knows the trade-off: more memory and slower reads for much faster contended writes

title: Producer-Consumer with Poison-Pill Shutdown
prompt:
Build a worker pipeline: many producers submit items, N consumer threads process them, and shutdown is graceful.

```java
class PoisonPillPipeline<T> {
  PoisonPillPipeline(int consumers, int capacity, Consumer<T> handler); // starts consumers
  void submit(T item) throws InterruptedException;   // blocks when full (backpressure)
  boolean shutdownAndAwait(long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws InterruptedException;
}
```

**Requirements**
- Every item successfully submitted before `shutdownAndAwait` is processed exactly once.
- Shutdown uses **poison pills**: one sentinel per consumer, enqueued after all accepted items; each consumer exits when it takes a pill.
- `submit` after shutdown begins throws `IllegalStateException`. Shutdown is idempotent.
- A handler that throws must not kill its consumer (otherwise a pill is never consumed and shutdown hangs).
- `shutdownAndAwait` returns false if consumers do not finish within the timeout.

**Allowed:** `ArrayBlockingQueue` / `LinkedBlockingQueue`, `Thread`. **Not allowed:** `ExecutorService`.

**Follow-ups:** Poison pill vs. interrupt vs. a volatile flag + poll(timeout). How do you handle multiple producers that each want to send a pill?
hints: Use a private static final Object as the pill so it can never equal a real item.
Put exactly one pill per consumer; a consumer that takes a pill returns without re-enqueueing it.
Make "check not shut down + enqueue" atomic with respect to "mark shut down + enqueue pills", so no item lands behind the pills.
keyPoints: Unique sentinel object (not null, not a magic value)
One pill per consumer; FIFO queue guarantees all earlier items drain first
Race between submit and shutdown closed (items never enqueued after pills)
Handler exceptions caught inside the loop; interruption restores the flag and exits
Bounded queue for backpressure; timed join honoring total timeout

title: Delayed Task Executor (DelayQueue-Style)
prompt:
Implement a single-worker scheduler that runs tasks after a delay - a tiny `ScheduledExecutorService`.

```java
class DelayedTaskExecutor {
  DelayedTaskExecutor();                                   // starts one worker thread
  void schedule(Runnable task, long delay, TimeUnit unit); // thread-safe
  void shutdown() throws InterruptedException;             // discard pending, join worker
}
```

**Requirements**
- A task never runs before its deadline, and runs promptly after it (no polling loops with `sleep`).
- Tasks run in deadline order (FIFO for equal deadlines).
- If a task with an *earlier* deadline is scheduled while the worker is sleeping toward a later one, the worker must wake and run the earlier task first.
- A throwing task must not kill the worker. Tasks run without holding the scheduler lock.
- After `shutdown`, `schedule` throws `IllegalStateException`.

**Allowed:** `PriorityQueue`, `ReentrantLock`, `Condition`, atomics. **Not allowed:** `DelayQueue`, `ScheduledExecutorService`, `Timer`.

**Follow-ups:** The leader/follower optimisation in DelayQueue for multiple workers; hierarchical timing wheels (Kafka, Netty) for millions of timers.
complexity: schedule O(log n); dispatching each task O(log n); O(n) memory.
hints: Min-heap keyed by nanoTime deadline (+ a sequence number for ties).
Worker: under the lock, peek; if empty await(); if not due, awaitNanos(remaining); else poll and run it outside the lock.
schedule() signals the condition only when the new task became the head of the heap.
keyPoints: Timed wait on a Condition (awaitNanos), re-checking the head after every wakeup
Signal when a new earliest task arrives (no oversleeping / missed preemption)
Overflow-safe nanoTime comparisons (a - b < 0)
Task executed outside the lock; exceptions caught so the worker survives
Clean shutdown: flag under lock, signal, join; rejects later schedules

title: Concurrent Web Crawler (Bounded Parallelism + Dedup)
prompt:
Implement a multithreaded crawler (LeetCode 1242 style, but with real termination and bounded concurrency).

```java
class WebCrawler {
  WebCrawler(Function<String, List<String>> fetchLinks, int parallelism); // fetchLinks is blocking I/O
  Set<String> crawl(String startUrl) throws InterruptedException;
  static String hostOf(String url);  // provided
}
```

**Requirements**
- Return every URL reachable from `startUrl` whose host equals the start URL's host (including `startUrl`).
- Each URL is fetched **at most once**, even when many pages link to it simultaneously.
- At most `parallelism` fetches run at any moment.
- `crawl` returns as soon as all work is finished - detect termination without sleeping or polling.
- A fetch that throws is treated as a page with no links; it must not hang or abort the crawl.
- No thread leaks: worker threads are shut down before `crawl` returns.

**Allowed:** `ExecutorService`, `ConcurrentHashMap`, atomics, `synchronized`/`wait`. Avoid parallel streams.

**Follow-ups:** Politeness (per-host rate limits), crawling across machines (URL frontier partitioned by host hash), using virtual threads + a Semaphore instead of a fixed pool.
complexity: O(V + E) work over reachable pages; O(V) memory for the seen set; wall time ~ (V / parallelism) * fetch latency.
hints: ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet().add(url) is an atomic "first one wins" dedup check.
A fixed thread pool of size parallelism bounds concurrent fetches.
Count pending tasks: increment before submitting a child, decrement when a task finishes; when it hits zero, the crawl is done.
keyPoints: Atomic dedup via set.add return value (no check-then-act race)
Pending counter incremented before child submission so it cannot reach zero early
Termination signaled via wait/notify or a latch, not sleep-polling
Bounded pool; executor shut down in finally (no thread leak)
Fetch failures handled inside the task; decrement in finally
